prompt: Create a photorealistic editorial photograph for the About section of YAT.lifestyle, an independent Hong Kong perfume brand founded by a biotechnology student. This is a conceptual atmospheric illustration, NOT documentary evidence of a real founder or actual premises. WIDE LANDSCAPE 3:2 composition, high resolution. Distinct from a macro pipette/test-tube scene and from a product bottle ad. A modest Hong Kong creative workspace just after sunset, photographed at bench height with a 50mm lens. On a deep charcoal tabletop in the lower central half: an open off-white working notebook with indistinct small pencil lines, a few long unprinted ivory perfume blotter strips arranged casually but purposefully, one small plain amber reagent bottle with a closed dark cap, and a dark glass dish. No pipette, no dropper, no rows of test tubes, no final perfume bottle design. At camera left, part of a tall old steel-framed apartment window; through it, closely spaced Hong Kong residential towers and a few warm illuminated windows recede into blue-black evening, recognizably dense Hong Kong rather than a landmark skyline. A warm desk lamp just OUTSIDE the frame illuminates the paper and creates a small, credible amber reflection in the glass. More intimate real student-scale working room than expensive laboratory. Editorial still life about the beginning of an idea: material, local, thoughtful, understated. Palette predominantly rich near-black and warm ivory, tiny champagne-gold light accents, muted blue-black outside. Honest paper fibre, worn matte tabletop, convincing glass, delicate uneven natural shadows. Avoid glossy CGI, fantasy architecture, giant bokeh circles, haze, heavy film grain, marble plinths, flowers, decorative fabric, jewellery, people, hands, logos, readable text, watermark. Keep all essential objects in the central 50 percent of the image width and middle 60 percent of its height so both a tall portrait crop and a wide crop remain coherent. Give a little breathing space around the tabletop. This should feel like an evocative photograph of a place where a fragrance idea begins, not a generic luxury product advertisement. No collage, no typography, no border.
